articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk hires Drew Rosenhaus in attempt to get wideout 'back to work and playing again in the NFL'
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk hasn't played in an NFL game since 2024.
articles.body:
It's been over two years since San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk played in an NFL game. After sustaining an ACL and MCL injury during the 2024 season, Aiyuk was initially placed on the PUP list ahead of 2025. But his relationship with the 49ers deteriorated, leading Aiyuk to not appear in a game despite still being under contract with the team.

Now the wideout is looking to change that. In an attempt to get back in the NFL, the 28-year-old Aiyuk hired agent Drew Rosenhaus, per multiple media reports. Rosenhaus told reporters he is tasked with "working on getting [Aiyuk] back to work and playing again in the NFL ."

Aiyuk was previously represented by agent Ryan Williams, but reportedly fired him last November. Aiyuk blamed Williams for the issues between the wideout and the 49ers.

In December, the 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left team list. He remains on there today.

Months after firing Williams, Aiyuk was vocal on social media, often expressing a desire to join the Washington Commanders. Aiyuk and Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels played together at Arizona State for one season. That trade never materialized.

If Aiyuk is serious about returning to the NFL, his path forward is unclear. With his relationship with the 49ers ruined, the wideout would first likely need to establish his intent to play again. It's unclear, however, if Aiyuk would be willing to report to the team if the 49ers required it.

It's also unclear how much interest teams have in Aiyuk. While he proved to be immensely talented in 2022 and 2023, he hasn't played in an NFL game in two seasons and spent the past offseason torpedoing his chances of a return to the 49ers.

Given the injury questions and his personal baggage, Aiyuk might not draw much interest on the trade market.

While the 49ers could use help at wide receiver due to the team's various injuries, it doesn't appear the team is willing to welcome Aiyuk back. When asked about that possibility in September, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan simply replied "no" when the option was discussed .

Aiyuk is still under contract with the 49ers through the 2028 season. He signed a four-year, $120 million extension with the team in 2024, just months before his season-ending knee injury.

articles.title: NFL news, live updates: Lions LB Jack Campbell remains hospitalized with neck injury; Cardinals bench Jacoby Brissett, will start Gardner Minshew in Week 9
articles.summary: Follow along with the latest NFL news coming out of Week 8.
articles.body: Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season is nearly a wrap, with just the Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks left to play on "Monday Night Football."There was plenty of excitement on Sunday, including two games that went into overtime, but they unfortunately weren't without injuries. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson made his return to the lineup after rehabbing an ankle injury, but that excitement was short-lived, as he suffered a thumb injury on his first pass attempt of the game. Per head coach Jesse Minter, he'll require surgery and a stint on the injured reserve list — a brutal blow. Backup Tyler Huntley is also dealing with what is thought to be a turf toe injury, which forced Baltimore to resort to their emergency third quarterback, Joe Fagnano. He completed 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards and an interception in relief of Jackson and Huntley this week.The Ravens are playing on a short week, as they're set to host the Jacksonville Jaguars on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 9.The Detroit Lions handed the Minnesota Vikings their first loss of the season, but lost a key playmaker on defense as All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a scary-looking neck injury. He was immobilized on a backboard before being transported to the hospital as his teammates gathered around him in an emotional scene.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 8.

articles.title: NFL rumors: Cardinals’ Jacoby Brissett benching sparks trade buzz with Ravens amid Lamar Jackson injury woes
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals have made a major change to their quarterback depth chart, and Jacoby Brissett could soon find himself with a new team. Despite Sunday...
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals have made a major change to their quarterback depth chart , and Jacoby Brissett could soon find himself with a new team. Despite Sunday's win over the Dallas Cowboys, Arizona has demoted Brissett to QB3, opening the door for potential trade discussions ahead of next week's deadline.

Gardner Minshew is now the Cardinals' starting quarterback after leading the Cardinals to a win on Sunday. Rookie Carson Beck has moved into the backup role.

According to NFL insider Ari Meirov, Brissett could become a trade target , with the Baltimore Ravens mentioned as a potential landing spot. Baltimore has dealt with serious injury concerns surrounding Lamar Jackson , as well as Tyler Huntley, making additional quarterback depth worth considering.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

There is also a familiar connection that could make the Ravens an interesting fit. Baltimore hired Israel Woolfork as its quarterbacks coach this offseason after he previously held the same role with Arizona. Woolfork has worked with Brissett before, which could make a potential move easier for the Ravens to evaluate. Brissett has experience and could provide Baltimore with another veteran option if the team feels they can still contend.

Meirov also mentioned Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent as another possible option for Baltimore. Bagent previously worked with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, giving the Ravens another familiar name to consider.

Nothing indicates that a Brissett trade is imminent, but his demotion makes the situation worth monitoring. Arizona appears comfortable moving forward with Minshew and Beck, while Baltimore could use another experienced quarterback as it navigates Jackson's injury concerns. With the deadline approaching, Brissett's future in Arizona is suddenly uncertain.
